body_md: Requirements 10k pastes daily with expiry. API POST /pastes and GET /:id in axum. Storage Postgres text plus Redis cache. Bottleneck random id guessing, snippet uses signed ids.
code:
let id: String = rand::thread_rng()
    .sample_iter(&Alphanumeric).take(8).collect();
hook: Pastebin on axum with expiry done right.
output:
id = 8 random alphanumerics, e.g. 'aZ3xQ9tB'
// unguessable; Postgres + Redis TTL expire it

quiz.explain: Random ids plus cache plus expiry cover the load.
options: Random IDs, Redis cache, TTL-driven cleanup
Sequential IDs so pastes are easy to find and list
Keep pastes forever since storage is cheap
Store each paste as a file on the app host
quiz.q: What are the key pastebin design choices?

takeaway: Use random identifiers with caching and expiry for paste storage.
trap: Using sequential ids that leak volume and invite scraping.

body_md: Requirements single-user todos with 5k writes daily. API CRUD /todos with validation in axum. Storage Postgres via sqlx with user index. Bottleneck N plus one lists, snippet pages by cursor.
code:
sqlx::query!("SELECT * FROM todos WHERE user_id=$1 AND id>$2 LIMIT 50",
    uid, cursor).fetch_all(&pool).await?
hook: Todo API that skips the N plus one trap.
output:
Ok(rows) // <= 50 todos via index (user_id, id) range scan
// needs live DB; no N+1, no OFFSET drift

quiz.explain: An indexed cursor seeks straight to the next page, so cost stays flat however deep the user scrolls.
options: Load every row, then paginate in Rust memory
Cursor pages on an index of (user_id, id)
OFFSET pages; Postgres skips rows for free
Fetch each todo by id in a loop over the list
quiz.q: How do you scale todo listing?

takeaway: Page todos by indexed cursor instead of loading full lists.
trap: Fetching all todos then filtering in application memory.

body_md: Requirements 50k background jobs daily with retries. API enqueue plus workers polling. Storage Postgres queue table with status index. Bottleneck double pickup, snippet uses SKIP LOCKED.
code:
SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE status='queued'
ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 10;
hook: Postgres job queue without double delivery pain.
output:
| id | 10 queued rows claimed |
| workers skip each other's locks; none picked twice |

quiz.explain: Locked skip lets workers claim without blocking peers.
options: LOCK TABLE so only one worker reads
SELECT then UPDATE status in two steps
Each worker polls with a random delay
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to claim rows
quiz.q: How do workers share a Postgres queue?

takeaway: Claim queued jobs with row locks that skip locked rows.
trap: Polling without locks and running jobs twice.

body_md: Requirements fan-out webhooks to 5k endpoints fast. API register hook plus event publish. Storage Postgres outbox plus Redis retry queue. Bottleneck slow receivers, snippet retries with backoff.

quiz.explain: Outbox plus bounded retry isolates slow endpoints.

Outbox, signed POSTs, bounded backoff retries
Fire once and drop any delivery that isn't 2xx
Retry forever at a fixed one-second pace

takeaway: Isolate slow receivers with signed posts and bounded retries.
trap: Blocking publishers while one receiver times out.

quiz.explain: Batched commits plus segment merge keep search fast.

takeaway: Batch index commits and merge segments for steady search speed.
trap: Committing the index on every single document.

body_md: Requirements mobile plus web clients evolving fast. API REST for CRUD and GraphQL gateway for screens. Storage same Postgres via dataloaders. Bottleneck N plus one resolvers, snippet batches loads.

body_md: Requirements internal RPC at 20k calls per second. API protobuf service with tonic. Storage Postgres plus Redis cache. Bottleneck missing deadlines, snippet layers tower timeouts.

body_md: Requirements 100k events daily with ordering choice. API produce and consume via client. Storage Kafka log or NATS JetStream. Bottleneck replay needs, snippet picks by retention.

// need replay + transactions -> kafka

quiz.explain: Kafka keeps long, partitioned logs built for replay; NATS (even with JetStream persistence) is lighter to run.

Kafka for long replay; NATS for light messaging

body_md: Requirements email login with sessions for 20k users. API POST /login and middleware guard. Storage Postgres users plus Redis sessions. Bottleneck timing leaks, snippet hashes with Argon2.

body_md: Requirements safe payment retries without double charge. API POST /pay with Idempotency-Key. Storage Postgres keyed request log. Bottleneck replay races, snippet locks per key.
code:

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING *; // replay stored

output:

// retries never double-charge

quiz.explain: Stored keyed responses make retries return same result.

takeaway: Store keyed responses and replay them on conflicting retries.
trap: Retrying payments without server-side idempotency keys.
